issues.legal_issue: An error in the survey numbers in a sale proclamation does not invalidate a sale when the property’s identity is otherwise clear and the error causes no prejudice.
material_facts: The proclamation misstated the survey numbers of two plots, but otherwise described their area, tenure, and other identifying details.
The owner testified that he knew which plots were being sold, and the evidence showed that no one was misled about their identity.
The court found the proclamation satisfied the applicable requirements for describing the land.
issues.conclusion: The sale was not invalidated by the erroneous survey numbers because the errors were misdescriptions, not mistaken identifications.
issues.legal_principle: Section 32(2) of the Travancore Revenue Recovery Regulation required a sale notice to specify the defaulter, the position, tenure and extent of the land and buildings, the revenue assessed, and the time, place and conditions of sale. Where the property’s identity is clear and there is only a misdescription, the error is an irregularity rather than a ground to treat the sale as having occurred without a proclamation. The Court applied Sheodhyan Singh v. Muhammat Kuer, [1962] 2 S.C.R. 753, and Thakur Barmha v. Jiban Ram Marwari, (1913) L.R. 41 I.A. 38.

rule.if: revenue_sale_challenged and survey_numbers_misstated and property_identity_clear and no_material_prejudice

predicates.revenue_sale_challenged: A party challenged the validity of a sale conducted to recover a debt through a revenue-sale process.
predicates.survey_numbers_misstated: The sale notice gave incorrect survey numbers for the land offered for sale.
predicates.property_identity_clear: The land’s area, tenure, or other identifying details made clear which property was being sold.
predicates.no_material_prejudice: The error did not mislead interested persons or cause material prejudice to the person challenging the sale.

issues.definition: When a revenue sale is challenged, incorrect survey numbers do not make the sale void if the property remains identifiable and the error causes no material prejudice.

issues.legal_issue: An assertedly inadequate sale price does not invalidate a sale without evidence that the property was worth substantially more or that the sale involved fraud.
material_facts: The appellant asserted that property said to be worth a much higher amount had been sold for a low price.
The evidence did not establish that the property was worth more than the value stated in the appellant’s own earlier account.
The property was subject to mortgages in favour of the government and private parties, and the trial court found no fraud.
issues.conclusion: The Court was not satisfied that the property had been sold at a low price and rejected this ground for invalidating the sale.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the claim of inadequate price against the evidence of the property’s value and its existing mortgage encumbrances. It found no proof of fraud and no adequate evidentiary basis to conclude that the sale price was low.

rule.if: revenue_sale_challenged and sale_price_claimed_inadequate and no_reliable_evidence_of_higher_value and property_subject_to_mortgages and fraud_not_proved

predicates.revenue_sale_challenged: A party challenged the validity of a sale conducted to recover a debt through a revenue-sale process.
predicates.sale_price_claimed_inadequate: The challenger asserted that the sale price was too low compared with the property's value.
predicates.no_reliable_evidence_of_higher_value: The evidence did not reliably establish that the property was worth substantially more than the value supported by the record.
predicates.property_subject_to_mortgages: The property was subject to mortgage interests when it was sold.
predicates.fraud_not_proved: The evidence did not establish fraud in connection with the sale.

issues.definition: A claimed inadequate price does not set aside a challenged revenue sale when the evidence does not establish a substantially higher value, the property is mortgaged, and fraud is not proved.

issues.legal_issue: A sale is not invalidated merely because revenue-recovery procedures were used where the objection that the debt was not recoverable as public or land revenue was raised only belatedly and the creditor could rely on a contractual power of sale.
material_facts: The appellant argued that the debt under the bond could not be recovered as arrears of public or land revenue because no written agreement provided for that method of recovery.
The objection had not been raised at an earlier stage, and the Court considered that the government might then have relied on the power of sale in the bond.
The sale used the procedures provided by the revenue-recovery regulation rather than an ad hoc procedure.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to set aside the sale on this ground and held that using the revenue-recovery machinery rather than ad hoc machinery did not itself invalidate the sale.
issues.legal_principle: Section 59 of the Travancore Revenue Recovery Regulation permitted recovery under the Regulation of specified government debts and sums made recoverable as public or land revenue by written agreement or another regulation. Although no such written agreement or other regulation was shown for the debt, the Court would not set aside the sale on an objection raised late when the government might have relied on a contractual power of sale had the objection been raised earlier. The use of the Regulation’s machinery did not itself vitiate the sale.

rule.if: revenue_sale_challenged and recoverability_objection_raised_late and bond_contains_power_of_sale and regulation_machinery_used

predicates.revenue_sale_challenged: A party challenged the validity of a sale conducted to recover a debt through a revenue-sale process.
predicates.recoverability_objection_raised_late: The objection that the debt could not be recovered through the revenue process was not raised at an earlier stage of the proceedings.
predicates.bond_contains_power_of_sale: The bond gave the creditor a power to sell property to recover the debt.
predicates.regulation_machinery_used: The sale was conducted using procedures established by a revenue-recovery regulation.

issues.definition: When the recoverability objection is raised late and the bond provides a power of sale, use of the revenue-recovery procedures alone does not invalidate the challenged sale.

issues.legal_issue: A sale of property not covered by the security is unauthorized, and selling that property together with secured property in one lot vitiates the entire sale.
material_facts: The bonds gave the government a power to sell only the properties identified as security.
Additional properties that were not given as security were attached and included in the sale.
The secured and non-secured properties were sold together in one lot.
issues.conclusion: The inclusion of non-secured properties in the single-lot sale vitiated the whole sale, and the sale of all the properties was declared void.
issues.legal_principle: A creditor’s contractual power of sale extends only to the properties identified as security in the bond. Because the secured and non-secured properties were sold together in one lot, the unauthorized inclusion vitiated the whole sale.

predicates.revenue_sale_challenged: A party challenged the validity of a sale conducted to recover a debt through a revenue-sale process.
predicates.nonsecured_property_included: The sale included property that had not been provided as security for the debt.
predicates.secured_and_nonsecured_property_sold_tog: The secured property and the property not provided as security were sold together as a single lot.

issues.definition: When a challenged revenue sale includes property outside the security and sells it together with secured property in one lot, the entire sale is void.
